alt: Poem 1 and Poem 2 are linked by two-way arrows at three levels: ideas and attitudes about the question’s focus, the methods each poet uses, and the different effects on the reader. A note says AO3 credit comes from the relationship between the poems.
caption: Strong answers compare ideas, methods and effects, not just content.

after: ## Theme clusters across the sixteen poems
alt: Six theme clusters on the left are linked to the sixteen anthology poems on the right: parents and children, childhood, death and suffering, love and loss, power and control, and identity and language. Piano, Do not go gentle into that good night, Remember and La Belle Dame sans Merci each belong to two clusters.
caption: Most poems fit more than one cluster, so revise them in pairs.

after: ## Form as a point of comparison
alt: Two sonnets drawn as fourteen lines each. Sonnet 116 builds an argument to a closing rhyming couplet; Remember turns after line 8, from request to permission in the sestet. Cards below name other anthology forms: a villanelle, a dramatic monologue, a ballad, and free or broken form.
caption: Compare how each poet uses a form, not just which form it is.

alt: An overview, then four comparison points, each setting Sonnet 116 beside Remember: constancy versus release, how each sonnet turns, time and death, and voice and the reader. Every row moves between both poems.
caption: Each paragraph is one point of comparison, with both poems in it.

alt: The guide’s sample sentence split into four labelled parts: the connective “Where”, a method in Sonnet 116 (the couplet), a method in Remember (the sestet), and the difference in effect. A row of other comparative connectives follows: whereas, similarly, in contrast, both, however, unlike.
caption: Connective, a method in each poem, and the difference it makes.

after: ## Worked example: choosing your own second poem
alt: Piano is named in a question on memory. Two possible partners branch from it: Poem at Thirty-Nine, with two adult speakers remembering a parent, and Half-past Two, with childhood memories in a very different tone. A checklist asks whether the second poem gives three comparable points, differs in method and is known well enough.
caption: Pick a partner that shares the focus but differs in method, and decide fast.
